- German-source income of the other period (§ 49 EStG; see de-non-resident-tax), for example rent from a German flat let before arrival (§ 2(7) sentence 3);
- the full basic allowance and the full employee lump sum: there is no cut by months for a resident assessment. Special expenses of the resident months are deducted as usual; for contributions paid in the other months see Cross-border points.

**Step 3: income that raises the rate.** These are left out of the base but added to find the rate (§ 32b(1) sentence 1):

- **No. 2: foreign income of the other period** that was not subject to German tax ("ausländische Einkünfte, die im Veranlagungszeitraum nicht der deutschen Einkommensteuer unterlegen haben"), for cases of part-year full liability, including § 2(7) sentence 3 cases. The official guidance confirms: on arrival or departure, income earned outside the period of full liability counts for the progression clause if it is not subject to limited liability (EStH 2025, H 32b "Zeitweise unbeschränkte Steuerpflicht").
- **No. 3: income a tax treaty exempts in Germany**, in the resident months (often foreign employment income or foreign rent).

**Exception for EU and EEA items under no. 3 only (§ 32b(1) sentence 2).** Treaty-exempt rent from property in another EU or EEA state, profits of an EU or EEA farm, and profits of an EU or EEA commercial establishment that fails the active-business test of § 2a(2), do not raise the rate. The exception is written for no. 3 only. Foreign rent of the months before arrival falls under no. 2 and raises the rate wherever the property is.

**Step 4: the amount added (§ 32b(2)).** Foreign income is computed under German rules: profit or surplus, not gross receipts. For foreign pay, the EUR 1,230 employee lump sum is deducted only to the extent it was not already deducted against German pay, and actual Werbungskosten only so far as all Werbungskosten together exceed the lump sum (§ 32b(2) sentence 2 (a) and (b)). Extraordinary income in it counts at one fifth. Foreign losses lower the rate and can bring it to zero (EStH 2025, H 32b "Ausländische Verluste"). Contributions to the Swiss AHV do not reduce the amount added (same, citing BFH 18 April 2012).

**Step 5: the tax.** Tariff tax on (taxable income + amount added), divided by that sum, cut to four decimal places of a percent = special rate. Special rate × taxable income, rounded down = income tax. Then the surcharge and church tax on that tax (de-income-tax).

**Joint assessment in the year of moving.** Spouses may choose it if both were fully liable and not permanently separated at some time in the year (§ 26(1) EStG). If both move together, the year qualifies.

## Deadlines and filing

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| Partnership return | Erklärung zur gesonderten und einheitlichen Feststellung (main form ESt 1 B, with Anlage FB for the partners and Anlage FE-G or FE-S for the income; names from the ELSTER 2025 guide). A partnership with legal capacity files it, and if it does not, each partner must; for one without legal capacity, each partner (§ 181(2) AO). Electronic only, unless the office allows paper for hardship (§ 181(2a) AO) |
| Partnership return deadline, own preparation | Seven months after year end (§ 149(2) AO, applied by § 181(1) AO): 31 July 2027 is a Saturday, so Monday 2 August 2027 (§ 108(3) AO) |
| Partnership return deadline, tax adviser | Last day of February of the second year after: 29 February 2028 (§ 149(3) no. 5 AO). The office can ask for it earlier (§ 149(4) AO) |
| Trade tax return of a commercial partnership | Same deadlines (§ 149(3) no. 3 AO); see de-trade-tax |
| Partner's own return | Deadlines in de-income-tax (2 August 2027, or 29 February 2028 with an adviser) |
| Changes flow through | A change to the determination changes the partner's assessment; a change to profit changes the trade tax base amount notice (§ 35b(1) GewStG) |
| Year of moving | One return for the whole year, on the normal deadlines in de-income-tax. Foreign pay of the other period goes on Anlage N-AUS (de-employee-income-tax). Arrival and departure dates and foreign income must be declared |

## Penalties and interest

- **Late partnership return (§ 152(6) and (7) AO).** The late-filing surcharge rules for tax returns apply. Amount: 0.0625% of the positive sum of the determined income for each started month late, at least EUR 25 a month, rounded down to whole euros, at most EUR 25,000 (§ 152(10) AO). It must be set if the return is not filed within 14 months after the end of the year (for 2026: by 29 February 2028), unless the deadline was extended (§ 152(2) and (3) no. 1 AO, applied by § 152(6)). The nil-tax let-outs of § 152(3) nos. 2 and 3 do not apply to this return. It is set first against the partnership if it has legal capacity (§ 152(4) sentence 3 AO).
- **Partner's own return.** Late filing, interest (0.15% a month from 1 April 2028) and late payment: see de-income-tax.

## The taxable base

### Step 1: is the person a commuter?

1. Residence: where does the person live under domestic law, and if both, where under art. 4(2)?
2. Place of work in the other state (protocol no. 5(a))?
3. Regular return: commuting days ÷ agreed working days must be at least 20%. As explained above, the protocol excludes leave and sickness from the working days for the non-return test but does not expressly extend that exclusion to this denominator; calculate both denominators and retain the stated source uncertainty where the result differs.
4. Non-return days: count only days that meet protocol no. 5(e) and (f), and compare with 60 or the reduced limit for part-year or part-time work. Add days from all jobs in the work state.
5. If both tests pass, art. 15a applies to the whole year's pay from that employment. If either fails, go to Step 3.

The employer certifies the non-return days on form Gre-3, stamped by the tax office for the place of work (protocol no. 5(j)). Where the employer finds at the year end, or when the job ends, that commuter status fails because of the non-return days, it sends the Gre-3 to the tax authority that collects the withholding, if possible within three months (Gre-3 note 2). The employee must give the employer the facts needed (protocol no. 5(j)).

### Step 2: the German assessment of a commuter (German resident)

- All the pay, including pay for days worked in Switzerland, is German employment income. Compute it as for any employee (de-employee-income-tax): gross pay less Werbungskosten or the employee lump sum, then special expenses.
- The 2026 tariff applies to taxable income, with the solidarity surcharge at 5.5% above the EUR 20,350 threshold of income tax (see de-employee-income-tax).
- The Swiss tax withheld, up to 4.5% of gross, is credited against German income tax as if it were German withholding (art. 15a(3)(a); § 36(2) no. 2 EStG). It is not capped under § 34c. The employer's certificate of gross pay and Swiss tax is the evidence (protocol no. 6).
- The Swiss employer withholds the lower of 4.5% and the Swiss tariff tax (Gre-1 note 6(b)). The commuter gives the employer the Gre-1 when starting work and when changing employer; the German tax office then renews it each year without a new application (Gre-1 notes 2 and 7).
